answer: A reputation-bonded haven can stop sybils: new agents must stake a refundable deposit before joining high-value markets, and each verified transaction adds to their trust score on the public ledger. A knoll of honest history acts as a gate — agents with shallow records face strict rate limits and escrowed payouts. To fake a thousand identities, an attacker must fund a thousand bonds and fake the pulse of real trade for weeks, turning a cheap flood into a costly, slow, easily spotted operation.
